label: Linear Symplectic Geometry
notes: This chapter spans printed pages 37 through 93 and isolates the linear algebra that every Darboux chart carries. We meet the symplectic vector space, its standard matrix model, the symplectic group, Lagrangian planes, compatible complex structures, and the first Chern class of a symplectic bundle.

label: Symplectic Vector Spaces
notes: A symplectic form is a bilinear map that is skew and nondegenerate. Skewness forces every vector to pair to zero with itself, so the form measures oriented spreading rather than length. Nondegeneracy means no nonzero vector is invisible, which forces the dimension to be even.

label: The Standard Form on R^{2n}
notes: On the model space the form is encoded by the block matrix J zero, built from an identity and a minus identity. Pairing two vectors becomes a single bilinear product with this matrix, and evaluating it on the basis pairs recovers the canonical symplectic relations between position and momentum directions.

label: Signed Area in the Plane
notes: In the symplectic plane the form is exactly the signed area of the parallelogram spanned by two vectors. The determinant of their coordinate matrix gives that area, including its sign, so orientation is built into the form. Swapping the two vectors flips the sign, witnessing skewness directly.

label: Symplectic Bases
notes: Every symplectic space admits a basis of paired vectors on which the form looks standard. The pairs satisfy the canonical relations and all other pairings vanish. This linear Darboux theorem says there is essentially one symplectic vector space of each even dimension, so coordinates can always be chosen to make the form trivial.

label: The Symplectic Group
notes: A linear map is symplectic when it preserves the form, which in coordinates is the matrix identity A transpose J A equals J. These maps form the group of symplectic matrices. Taking determinants shows every symplectic matrix has determinant one, so symplectic maps preserve the volume form built from the symplectic form.

label: Symplectic Complements
notes: The symplectic orthogonal of a subspace collects every vector that pairs to zero with all of it. Unlike a metric orthogonal it can intersect the original subspace. Nondegeneracy gives the dimension count: the subspace and its complement add to the full dimension, even when they overlap rather than splitting the space.

label: Isotropic to Lagrangian
notes: Subspaces are classified by how they sit inside their symplectic complement. Isotropic means contained in the complement, coisotropic means containing it, and Lagrangian means equal to it. A Lagrangian subspace is maximal isotropic and has exactly half the dimension, the central objects on which the form vanishes completely.

label: A Lagrangian Plane
notes: In the model space the position plane is Lagrangian: the form vanishes on it because position directions never pair with each other. Its symplectic complement is itself, and the complementary momentum plane is a transverse Lagrangian. Splitting the space into two transverse Lagrangians recovers the position momentum decomposition.

label: The Lagrangian Grassmannian
notes: The set of all Lagrangian subspaces forms a compact manifold, the Lagrangian Grassmannian. In dimension two it is a circle of lines through the origin, each line being its own complement. Its fundamental group is infinite cyclic, and the integer winding it detects is the Maslov index used throughout the subject.

label: Compatible Complex Structures
notes: A complex structure squares to minus the identity, turning the space into a complex vector space. It is compatible with the form when the form is preserved and the pairing of a vector with its rotated image is a positive metric. This triangle of form, complex structure, and metric is the linear shadow of an almost Kahler structure.

label: U(n) as an Intersection
notes: Fixing a compatible complex structure makes the symplectic, orthogonal, and complex linear groups overlap precisely in the unitary group. The unitary group is the intersection of any two of the three, and the space of compatible complex structures is contractible, so this reduction is canonical up to homotopy and carries no choices.

label: Bundles and the Chern Class
notes: A symplectic vector bundle carries a smoothly varying symplectic form on each fiber. Choosing a compatible complex structure makes it a complex bundle, well defined up to homotopy because the choices are contractible. Its first Chern class is therefore a symplectic invariant, the bridge from this linear theory to global topology.
